subject.title: [Security] Arbitrary file read via symlink dereferencing in diagnostics exporter

question: Can any actor below the local operator trust boundary create or replace the config, configured log, or selected stability file that diagnostics export reads, and must those inputs therefore reject symlinks?
rationale: Source inspection disproves the reported recursive-workspace packaging model but cannot decide whether configured diagnostic input paths are intended to trust symlinks; that is a repository security-boundary decision.

options.title: Require regular files
options.body: Reject symlinks for every diagnostics input and add focused config, log, stability, and race-resistant regression coverage.

options.title: Keep trusted-path behavior
options.body: Document that diagnostics reads operator-selected files and close after proving no lower-trust actor can replace those paths.

options.title: Request concrete exploit proof
options.body: Keep the issue pending until the reporter supplies exact setup, attacker capability, symlink path, command, and leaked archive entry.

recommendation.title: Require regular files
recommendation.body: Reject symlinks for every diagnostics input and add focused config, log, stability, and race-resistant regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest available recent history around diagnostics privacy and filesystem/security boundaries.
